page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 physical cores configured with hyper-threading to deliver 8 dedicated vCPUs, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. The hardware setup includes 16.0 GB of memory, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, and AES-NI. The instance operates under the KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. It contains no onboard local storage and does not include GPU accelerators, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution in multi-threaded environments, reflected in a Passmark CPU score of 8266.91 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 4486. Memory subsystem performance shows sustained throughput, recording 50.07 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 37.35 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET operations reached 6.8 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 6.74 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded performance registers lower relative metrics, with stress-ng single-core output, single-thread gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression ranking in the bottom quartile.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers compute density suited for CPU-bound tasks where large memory footprints are not justified. The trade-off centers on weaker single-core processing speed and reliance on remote storage latency, which may affect storage-intensive I/O profiles. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.2xlarge is technically aligned with workloads such as parallel software builds using Clang, multi-threaded web application hosting, backend microservices, and general compute-driven API processing.

It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes AVX-512 with VNNI instructions, a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies on external block storage as no local disk is bundled. Benchmark profiles indicate solid multi-core processing performance, recording average scores across Passmark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Redis operations. Conversely, single-threaded throughput and compression tests place in lower percentiles. With balanced compute allocation and lack of dedicated GPU hardware, the ecs.c6e.2xlarge fits multi-threaded web serving, CI/CD code compilation, and distributed application processing workloads where high memory density is unnecessary.
